planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; transplant after frost risk passes; stake or cage firmly as an indeterminate variety known for good crack resistance.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost date and transplant into warm, fertile soil once frost danger has passed. Druzba is a Bulgarian heirloom whose name means 'friendship,' prized for combining an unusually early harvest window with the deep, balanced flavor more typical of longer-season tomatoes. The smooth, red, slightly flattened globes resist cracking better than many heirlooms and the vigorous indeterminate vines stay productive over a long season. Stake or cage securely and pinch suckers lightly to keep the sprawling growth manageable.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; this potato-leaved, indeterminate variety needs sturdy staking to support its large fruit and long season.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into deeply worked, fertile soil after frost risk has passed. Marianna's Peace is a Czechoslovakian family heirloom carried to the United States after World War II and later introduced commercially in honor of the woman whose story gave the variety its name. The potato-leaved, indeterminate vines produce large pink beefsteak fruit with a rich, well-balanced sweet flavor and relatively few seeds. Give it sturdy staking and a full growing season, as the heavy fruit and long maturity window reward patient care.

common_name: Hungarian Heart Tomato (Large Pink Oxheart Heirloom)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; the pointed oxheart fruit is heavy and low-seeded, so stake this indeterminate vine firmly.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into rich, well-drained soil once nights stay reliably warm. Hungarian Heart is an oxheart-type heirloom traced to a village near Budapest around 1900, valued for producing pointed, meaty pink fruit that often exceeds a pound with very few seeds and little core. The dense flesh and low moisture content make it especially good for sauces and canning as well as fresh slicing. Stake the vigorous indeterminate vines well, since the heavy fruit clusters can pull down unsupported branches.

common_name: Rose de Berne Tomato (Swiss Heirloom Pink Slicer)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; a vigorous 6-8 foot indeterminate vine that needs firm staking and shows good resistance to cracking.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil after frost risk passes. Rose de Berne is a classic heirloom from the Bern region of Switzerland, often described as the European counterpart to Brandywine for its reputation as one of the best-tasting pink tomatoes grown in France, Germany, and Switzerland. The smooth, deep-rose fruit has thin but durable skin and creamy, richly sweet-tart flesh. The vigorous 6-8 foot vines need firm staking and reward a long warm season with heavy, reliable yields.

common_name: Black Sea Man Tomato (Compact Russian Heirloom Beefsteak)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; this compact, potato-leaved variety needs only modest staking and suits containers or small gardens.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into warm, fertile soil after frost danger passes. Black Sea Man is a Russian heirloom with distinctive potato-leaf foliage and a naturally compact habit that makes it a good choice for smaller gardens or large containers where full-sized indeterminate vines would be unwieldy. The mahogany-brown fruit has olive-green shoulders and deep, marbled flesh with a rich, smoky-sweet flavor. Modest staking is usually enough to support the shorter, sturdier plants through their production window.

common_name: Ferris Wheel Tomato (1894 Salzer's Heirloom Pink Beefsteak)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; a tall, regular-leaf indeterminate vine that needs sturdy staking to carry its large flattened fruit.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into deeply prepared soil once all frost risk has passed. Ferris Wheel is an 1894 commercial release from the John A. Salzer Seed Company of Wisconsin that nearly vanished before being rediscovered and reintroduced by heirloom tomato researchers in the 1990s. It produces large, slightly flattened pink beefsteak fruit with colorful shoulders that blush attractively as they ripen, and the flesh is juicy, mild, and slightly sweet. Provide sturdy staking for the tall, regular-leaf indeterminate vines, which can exceed six feet over a 90-day season.

planting.note: Start indoors 12-16 weeks before transplanting; surface sow without covering since seed needs light to germinate. Chantilly performs best under the cool temperatures and short days of fall, winter, or early spring cut-flower production.

directions: Surface-sow the fine seed indoors under bright light 12-16 weeks before the intended transplant date, since snapdragon seed needs light to germinate and should not be covered. Chantilly is a cut-flower snapdragon series distinguished by open-faced blooms that stay flat rather than closing into the pinched 'dragon mouth' of traditional types, a form florists favor for its softer look in arrangements. It performs best under the cool temperatures and short days of fall, winter, or early spring production rather than the heat of summer, and can be grown either as a single tall stem or pinched for multiple cutting stems. Available in shades from bright white and cream-yellow to salmon, bronze, and deep purple, it is best suited to mild-winter or high-tunnel cut-flower operations.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

common_name: Madame Butterfly Snapdragon (Double Azalea-Flowered Cut-Flower Mix)

planting.note: Start indoors 12-16 weeks before transplanting; surface sow without covering since seed needs light to germinate. An All-America Selections winner grown for fully double, azalea-shaped blooms.

directions: Surface-sow the fine seed indoors under bright light 12-16 weeks before transplanting, since it needs light to germinate and should be left uncovered. Madame Butterfly is an All-America Selections-winning snapdragon series notable for fully double, azalea-shaped blooms that give the flower spikes a ruffled, almost rose-like appearance quite different from the single spurred flowers of classic snapdragons. The 24-30 inch plants are widely adapted and bloom in a broad color range including red, pink, orange, yellow, purple, and white, making dense, showy spikes prized for cutting. Like other snapdragons it thrives in cool weather and fades once summer heat sets in, so plan for a spring or fall harvest window.

common_name: Whirligig Zinnia (Picotee Bicolor Cut-Flower Zinnia Mix)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost when soil is warm; thin to spacing for good air circulation. Whirligig is grown for its picotee bicolor petal pattern, which gives blooms a pinwheel-like look.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost once the soil has warmed, thinning seedlings so plants have good air circulation. Whirligig is a zinnia mix known for its picotee patterning, where each semi-double to double bloom carries a contrasting band or tip color around the petal edge, giving the flowers a pinwheel-like look that sets it apart from solid-colored zinnia types. The bushy, roughly 20-inch plants produce abundant 3-4 inch flowers over a long summer season and respond well to regular cutting or deadheading. Like other zinnias it draws butterflies reliably and performs best in hot, sunny conditions with soil that isn't kept constantly wet.

planting.note: Direct sow after frost in average soil; overly rich soil reduces blooms. Cupcake is grown for its unusual fused petals, which form a shallow cup around the central stamens.

directions: Direct sow into average to lean, well-drained soil after the last frost, since overly rich soil favors foliage over flowers. Cupcake is an unusual cosmos selection in which the outer petals fuse along their edges into a shallow cup or chalice shape, resembling a fluted cupcake wrapper around the central boss of gold stamens, a distinctly different form from the flat, open-faced blooms of typical cosmos. It flowers over a long season atop tall stems held above finely cut, ferny foliage, and its unusual shape makes it a conversation piece in cutting gardens and pollinator borders alike. The plants rarely need staking despite their height and continue blooming into fall with regular deadheading.
